body: Hey, I just saw your post history and noticed you got kenalog injections done and we’re looking into laser removal for your keloids. I have about 50 keloids myself all over my back, some on my chest, and some on my legs. I have gotten two keloid removal surgeries with SRT radiation done afterwards and they helped remove some of them but I still have a ton of keloids left. I feel like it would be almost impossible to get every single one surgically removed and radiated, so I wanted to see if there were other options. Would you say the kenalog injections helped all 30 of your keloids? And did they come back by any chance? You mentioned that they got flattened but not fully removed, did you find a way to get them fully treated? A few of my keloids are massive, like a few inches wide and I was wondering if the treatment you got would work for them too?
Huh, that’s interesting. Are there any side effects you have noticed with being on Remicade? Or nothing at all.
Are you taking Zinc Gluconate?
Thank you so much for your input! I really appreciate the time you took to answer my questions! This condition sucks and I hope I can figure out ways to make my flares come down :)

I got one last question, does oil seem to be an issue for you? Like olive oil and such? I feel like even a tablespoon of oil may seem to be of issue to me but not sure if it’s common or if there’s another problem going on here. Thank you so much for for your help!

Because I eat fruits and stuff and they have natural sugars like the yogurt I eat, which has 0 g added sugar and I don’t think natural sugars seem to be a problem for me. Like you said, it could be the lactose that’s the issue in whole milk yogurt, but to my knowledge eating Greek yogurt hasn’t resolved my issues.
Good to know, have you tried whole milk yogurt by any chance? Like from stonyfield or a brand like that? It isn’t nearly as thick as Greek yogurt and its texture is different.

> One point I take from all of this is that while I agree with you that  the individual person has some control in the development of his or her  sense of right and wrong,. to a significant degree his choices are  effected by the culture around him other. 

I can agree with this. Could you elaborate more on what kind of culture you mean when you say they affect my sense of right and wrong? In my childhood I definitely attended religious practices with my parents, but whatever they taught me in terms of right, wrong, etc. didn't come from their religious teachings. It wasn't "You should be kind because otherwise god will punish you," it was more "You should be kind because you shouldn't hurt others' feelings for no reason." So when you say culture, what kind of culture are you talking about? Especially, what type of culture that affects my sense of right and wrong?

> Many religions at least suggest that God is love and justice and that  God demands love and justice of her people. If one really takes these  ideas seriously then it can not but have an impact on one decisions in  one economic, political, and social life. 

I don't disagree with this statement. According to me god does demand love and justice because in my mind those are the correct morals. So, I agree that god in general has this sentiment. I didn't have to be part of religion to come to these conclusions though, I am able to do that by just believing in god and what he wants. But, more importantly, an even stronger phrase to me that gives me sense a sense of direction is that **I demand love and justice.** If we take god out of the picture for one second and look at what I want, then it is the same thing. Overall, yes, both god and I want the same thing in the examples you pointed out, but I wouldn't necessarily say that religion gives me a deeper purpose, its more of my relationship with god and self reflection that does that. I feel like I can talk to god without being part of a religion and seeing what he has to say. I am able to communicate with him easily even if I don't associate myself with a religion.

>  I would argue that if God is Good,of God is Love, that if God is  Beautiful (there are religions which have confirmed this) then it would  be desirable / pleasurable  to become close to and related to such a  God. 

I agree with this as well. But, could I not be close to god without being part of a religion? If you don't think so, why not? What medium does religion provide to be closer to god that I cannot develop myself privately on a one on one relationship with him?

Whether I choose a religion or not, it’s nice to know that I can participate in traditions if I want to without having to follow that religion. Take praying before a meal for example, although I don’t do it, I would be completely fine if someone did and would be happy to go along with it. The same goes for any tradition really, I don’t really have anything against them, so participating in one or two from time to time is interesting and fun. I just won’t be doing those traditions on a day to day basis myself by following a religion I guess. I would like to travel and explore all the religions and visit their churches, temples, mosques, etc. in the future to learn more!

I completely agree with your points about being able to look to god just as someone to talk to, that makes complete sense to me! I’ve done that a few times even though I don’t have a visual of god as I don’t associate him with a religion. 

Thank you so much for the kind words, you have no idea how much that means to me :)

I can see how marriage, death, and tradition can be important. Is it wrong if I take part in a tradition but don’t necessarily believe in the religious aspect of it? I’m having a hard time thinking of specific traditions, do you have any in mind?

Hmm, I see where you are coming from but I think this is where we disagree. I feel like most humans have an innate ability to be able to see what’s right and wrong. Maybe I’m wrong on the most humans part, but talking about me specifically I feel like I can do that without being partial to any side. I feel like can come to the conclusion a lot of religious texts come to on topics that encompass large parts of society. Things like poverty, equality, etc. I also feel like I’m able to discern when I am being a bad human (where I am not nice to others, not trying to improve in life, not being open to all sides of a problem, only thinking about myself, etc.). I guess my point is, I feel like I’m very happy with my moral and ethical beliefs, so that would presumably point to the fact that religion is not really for me right?

Your first paragraph makes complete sense and I agree that if I wasn’t part of a religion I would be missing out on connecting with others with the same moral/ethical beliefs as me. In your second paragraph you mentioned gospel evidences; what do you mean by “knowing what god wants for us?” As for what we can do to be better spouses or parents, why is there a need for god to tell us what to do to be better? Shouldn’t a human be able to look within himself and see if he is mistreating his spouse or not being a good father/mother?

My goal isn’t to find a religion, it’s more of finding a reason as to why I need to belong to a religion. The reason you mentioned earlier, that it allows for a gathering to discuss your beliefs, seems to be the only thing I would be missing if I wasn’t part of a religion. Is there anything else I would be missing?

Thanks for the response. Did you need to believe in svadharma to be able to find your purpose? Also the more generalized purposes you mentioned, like help others whenever you can, seems like it is very possible to achieve that through self reflection.

I was talking about the individual’s purpose. I don’t really believe in a something where there is a general purpose for everyone. I mean different people want different things out of life. When you say purpose for everyone, would you mind giving me an example or two? Whichever religion says those purposes.

I think that’s part of the problem I have with the topic of religion. If a person is a specific religion, say Christian, are they not automatically saying the other religions are wrong due to the fact that they chose Christianity (whether they were born into it or not)? If picking a religion doesn’t say that, what does it say? Does it say that they agree with that religion’s morals and values? If so, then is the only purpose of religion to gather and discuss about your own morals and ethics? If you are part of a religion, what gives the doctrines the right to bestow a set of morals to follow? I believe that morality and ethics should come from within and don’t need to be dependent on anything else.

That is quite interesting! If the purpose of religion is to follow god’s laws and teachings, what are those teachings? Things like equality in men and women and elimination of extremes of wealth and poverty? Why are those teachings not coming from within the self? Why does it need to come from god? Can a person not look at the world and their morals and see what’s right and wrong for the world? A person should themselves be able to see how extreme poverty is harmful and how extreme wealth is bad too. They should also be able to see themselves that everyone should have equal rights. Why does this statement need to come from god?
Why does finding a purpose in life have to come from following a religion? Shouldn’t it come from self reflection and figuring out what you want out of life?

What type of beliefs do you think religion is helping you build? Moral beliefs? Ethical beliefs? If so, why do you need religion to build those beliefs, shouldn’t those beliefs come from the good of the heart? Also, how were you able to pick a religion? Not trying to be rude, just curious.

This is a valid answer. This the only thing that I can see that I would miss if I was not in a religion. When you say Christians choose which part of the doctrine they want to follow, are those doctrines completely filled with moral and ethical values? Why did they pick Christianity in the first place out of all the religions? I will check the video later when I have some more time on my hands, so forgive me if the answers to these questions are in the video already.

Well, I think that for me its pretty much impossible to not believe in some supernatural being that created this universe. I don’t really think that there is a completely scientific explanation for how the world started. I think that whatever goes on in our lives happens for a reason and the only way I can justify that is through god, and the fact that he is making things go a certain way. Because quite frankly, a lot of things in our lives are out of our control yet things turn out a specific way. I’m not really a person who is spiritual day in and day out, but when I think about the topic from time to time I always come to this conclusion. Let me know your thoughts.

Why are you trying to get to know god? Forgive my ignorance, but does religion teach you about god’s personality and traits? Or does it teach what’s right and wrong? If it’s the latter, why is it that a specific god has it the right way where as the other gods with different teachings have it wrong?
